title: Is creating dead games allowed?
author: EvilPugs
selftext:
I was playing game and I really enjoyed it before developers shut it down because they wanted version 2, but that failed miserably.

Not sure from legal perspective if I can/should copy the mechanics and have my own design and story.  Would that be fine or discouraged?

comments.author: imlo2
comments.body:
No one can stop you from making very similar game, but you can't clone the likeness and things too closely. Copyrights and trademarks will come into play in that case. It's always a bit of a grey area what is "too close" to another product to be a copyright violation, etc. 

And there's also the gamer aspect, how it's perceived, i.e. a cheap clone of game X, or something else?

comments.author: Proper_Front_1435
comments.body:
Are you talking about Kerbal? 

Could you make a space launching game with good physics. sure. 

If you do like... the kerbal characters? Probably gonna take some heat.

comments.author: Interesting-Yellow-4
comments.body:
Gameplay itself cannot be trademarked/copyrighted.  
Assets, systems, names, etc, those need to be distinct.

comments.author: re-skob
comments.body: yes, it's allowed, just make it your own

comments.author: Prestigious_Edge_472
comments.body: Since you're talking about copying the mechanics, you're 100% allowed even if it's not dead. There are hardly any games that are originals, the majority are just a xyz-like or mash between xyz and zyx. I would advise you to see what players didn't like about the original game and change it if you do make it though, who knows, you could come up with something even more fun and more refined.

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body:
You can make the game part but you can't copy the characters or the name. This is actually a very common practice in the game industry. I would say don't copy any code either.

For example, there is a popular game called Tower of Fantasy, where a developer said he'd loved the game Genshin Impact so much but wanted a more science fiction world, and he didn't feel much shame in directly copying a majority of the code and game mechanics. (I also personally prefer Tower of Fantasy to Genshin Impact.) BUT a lot of the gameplay from Genshin Impact was copied from Breath of the Wild. Pocketpair admitted in an interview to copying mechanics from ALL the games they love with Craftopia, including Breath of the Wild.

In true rags-to-riches form, the team of six people at Pocketpair hired on a new team to make Palworld, nearly copying all of the mechanics of Craftopia into Unreal Engine 5, and making them one of the industry-leading games in history. They also used lots of Ai in the making of Palworld, before Steam required the Ai disclaimer tag.

Just the same, because some of the Pals looked closely to Pokemon, they were sued several times by Nintendo for copyright infringement and many other things. Nintendo surprisingly lost most of the claims, but it should be noted to any observer to be careful when recreating works.
